documents.title: Introduction to Quantum Computing
documents.content:
# Qubits

A qubit is represented using the Bloch sphere. Superposition is a fundamental principle of quantum mechanics. Superposition enables quantum parallelism. Quantum entanglement is a correlation between qubits that has no classical counterpart.

# Algorithms

Shor's algorithm uses the quantum Fourier transform. Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) is a prerequisite for Shor's algorithm. Grover's algorithm was developed by Lov Grover. Quantum decoherence prevents reliable computation on large devices.

Quantum computing is defined as computation that exploits quantum-mechanical phenomena such as superposition and entanglement.

documents.title: Qubits Explained for Teachers
documents.content: Qubits are represented using the Bloch sphere, a geometric picture of a two-level system. The Bloch sphere is a geometric representation of a single qubit state. Measurement causes the collapse of the superposition. Quantum gates are part of quantum circuits. A Hadamard gate is a type of quantum gate that creates superposition from a basis state.
